key_insight: In solid molecular hydrogen, including multiple particle–hole transitions in QMC barely changes excitation energies but is crucial for predicting exciton localization and related response properties.
engineering_relevance: Accurate modeling of excitonic localization, optical transitions, and excitation-induced forces requires wave functions beyond a single orbital substitution, especially in the low-density insulating regime.
method: Model the lowest neutral excitation in phase-I molecular hydrogen under increasing compression using QMC.
Compare single-substitution and multideterminant excited-state wave functions against BSE and TDDFT.
Evaluate nuclear configurations representing thermal and quantum fluctuations.
evidence_signal: Across sampled nuclear configurations, multideterminant QMC generally agrees with BSE on localization, transition dipoles, and excitation-induced forces, while TDDFT predicts more extended excitons; differences diminish under compression.
watch_item: Excitation-energy agreement alone does not validate localization or response predictions, which can differ substantially between methods for particular nuclear configurations.
paper_title: Excitons in solid molecular hydrogen from quantum Monte Carlo
